# NumberStamp

Namespace `Nfty.Core.Imaging` in assembly `Nfty.Core`.

```csharp
public static class NumberStamp
```

Stamps an asset's set number into a corner, for telling loose sprites apart.

## Remarks

**The digits are PIXELS, not a typeface, and that is the whole design.** Every image this project touches is generated pixel art shown at a size unrelated to its pixel count, and nothing anywhere resamples, blurs or anti-aliases. A real font would need `SixLabors.Fonts` and `ImageSharp.Drawing` — a new dependency beside an ImageSharp deliberately pinned at 3.1.11 — and would render a grey, anti-aliased number onto art that has no grey in it. A 3x5 bitmap font is twelve constants, needs nothing, and scales by an integer factor, so a stamped asset is still exactly the kind of image the rest of the product promises.

**It is a DEBUG mark and it is destructive, so it only ever happens on the way out.** Nothing here writes back into a Set: the export renders a stamped copy and ships that, which is why the same option cannot quietly corrupt the author's collection. The number stamped is the asset's own set number, so a folder of loose sprites sorts and cross-references against `nfty/NNNN.json` without anything else being recorded.

**White on black, both drawn.** An asset can be any colour, including white, and a bare white number vanishes on pale art while a bare black one vanishes on dark art. The glyph is drawn in white over a one-pixel black halo, which is legible on every ground and costs nothing but a second pass over the same cells.

## Methods

### Draw(Image&lt;Rgba32&gt;, int, StampCorner, int?) { #m-draw-sixlabors-imagesharp-image-sixlabors-imagesharp-p-5e7ea9 }

```csharp
public static void Draw(Image<Rgba32> image, int number, StampCorner corner, int? scale = null);
```

Draws a number into one corner of an image, in place.

**Parameters**

- `image` (`Image<Rgba32>`) - The image to stamp. Modified.
- `number` (`int`) - The number to draw. Negative is drawn as its absolute value.
- `corner` (`StampCorner`) - Which corner it sits in.
- `scale` (`int?`) - Font pixel size, or null for [`NumberStamp.ScaleFor()`](Nfty.Core.Imaging.NumberStamp.md#m-scalefor-system-int32-system-int32).

**Remarks**

**It draws nothing rather than clipping** when the stamp will not fit the canvas. A half-drawn number is worse than none: the point of the mark is that it can be read, and a "12" cropped to "1" on a tiny sprite is a wrong answer rather than a missing one.

### ScaleFor(int, int) { #m-scalefor-system-int32-system-int32 }

```csharp
public static int ScaleFor(int canvasWidth, int canvasHeight);
```

How large one font pixel is drawn on a canvas of this size.

**Parameters**

- `canvasWidth` (`int`) - The art's width.
- `canvasHeight` (`int`) - The art's height.

**Returns.** An integer scale, at least 1.

**Remarks**

**Derived rather than chosen, and capped at both ends.** A stamp fixed at one pixel is invisible on a 1000px asset and a stamp fixed at eight covers a 16px one entirely. A thirty-secondth of the short side keeps it roughly the same fraction of the picture at every canvas size; the floor of 1 is what a small sprite needs and the ceiling of 8 is where a debug mark stops being a mark and starts being the image.
